title: Reading and Listening Priority
summary: A 42-day recovery plan for learners whose Reading and/or Listening bands sit at least half a band below their Writing and Speaking (overall 3.5–5). Most hours go to Complete the Words, academic passages, campus listening and academic talks, with vocabulary in families and short productive maintenance.

schedule_json.split: About 70% Reading and Listening, 30% Writing and Speaking maintenance
daily_routine: 15 minutes: vocabulary in families with collocations (academic words)
20 minutes: one Complete the Words paragraph plus one Daily Life or academic reading set
20 minutes: one listening set (alternate short exchanges and academic talks)
10 minutes (alternate days): one Listen and Repeat set or one Build a Sentence set

weeks.label: Week 1 · Baseline and receptive audit
tasks: Full mock 1 in the TOEFL simulator; record all four section bands.
Audit Reading misses by task type: Complete the Words, Read in Daily Life, Read an Academic Passage.
Audit Listening misses by task type: Choose a Response, Conversation, Announcement, Academic Talk.
Note where misses cluster in each section (early or late) because Reading and Listening are two-stage adaptive.
Set up the vocabulary notebook by word family.
Weekly review: choose the first focus (Reading or Listening) from the audit.

checkpoint.target: Gap between receptive and productive sections confirmed (0.5 band or more)

weeks.label: Week 2 · Complete the Words and word families
tasks: One Complete the Words drill a day from the Complete the Words Drills guide, in level order, misses logged by type.
Study the suffix and small-word sections; make one family list per day from your misses.
Two Read in Daily Life sets; write the writer's purpose before answering.
Two Listen and Choose a Response sets with reply-type labels.
One Build a Sentence set and one Listen and Repeat set for maintenance.
Weekly review.

checkpoint.measure: Complete the Words accuracy per drill

weeks.label: Week 3 · Academic passages and purpose
tasks: Four academic passages: write one function label per paragraph before answering.
Stance mapping on two passages: author's view, reported view or evidence.
Drills 8–10 (level 3) from the Complete the Words Drills guide.
Section mock: Reading in simulator practice; review it with the full protocol.
One email and one interview for maintenance.
Weekly review.

checkpoint.target: Reading at least half a band above baseline, or R-purpose and R-infer entries halved

weeks.label: Week 4 · Campus listening and academic talks
tasks: Three conversation sets: predict the next action before the questions.
Three announcement sets: note the changed detail and the action required.
Four academic talks with two-word notes for purpose and structure; one play only.
Rotate accents: one session each of North American, British and Australian speakers.
Section mock: Listening in simulator practice; review it.
Weekly review.

checkpoint.target: Listening at least half a band above baseline, or L-structure and L-detail entries halved

weeks.label: Week 5 · Full mock 2 and the hardest material
tasks: Full mock 2 in the TOEFL simulator.
Recount receptive error categories (R-form, R-vocab, R-purpose, R-infer, L-reply, L-detail, L-structure).
Drills 11–12 (level 4) from the Complete the Words Drills guide, timed.
Two sessions on the largest remaining category.
Check Writing and Speaking have not dropped; add a maintenance session if they have.
Weekly review; start the Final 14 Days guide if your test is two weeks away.

checkpoint.measure: Mock 2 bands for all four sections
checkpoint.target: Gap between receptive and productive sections smaller than at baseline

weeks.label: Week 6 · Consolidate and perform
tasks: Two mixed timed sets: one Reading and one Listening, with extra care on the first items.
Write the top-ten error list, weighted toward Reading and Listening.
Logistics: ID, recipients, equipment check (Home Edition) or route (test center).
Light practice only in the last three days.
Test day, or continue with the Eight-Week Standard plan if mock 2 showed the gap is still large.

checkpoint.target: No new error categories; early-item misses rare

decision_rules: If R-vocab dominates after week 3, add 15 minutes a day of reading longer academic texts and record new words in families.
If misses cluster early in a section, slow the first items down slightly in every practice set.
If Writing or Speaking drops by half a band, add two maintenance sessions a week.

metadata.primary_focus_note: focus_section holds one value; this plan covers reading and listening (see focus_sections)
metadata.entry_rule: Reading and/or Listening at least 0.5 band below Writing and Speaking
metadata.recommended_for: Profile B learners: productive skills strong, receptive skills weaker.
metadata.score_window_basis: score_min/score_max are the ETS 0-120 comparison totals for band 3.5 (58+) and the top of band 5.5 (113); band windows are in band_*
metadata.guarantee: none: practice plan, not a score prediction
